newsitem.title: CROATIA: Former minister appointed to head Croat oil firm.
newsitem.headline: Former minister appointed to head Croat oil firm.

text.p: Croatian Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa said on Monday the current Economy Minister Davor Stern would be appointed to head the national oil firm INA Industrija Nafte.
"Minister Stern has experience in this field," Matesa was quoted by Croatian radio as telling reporters.

Matesa gave no time for the proposed reshuffle but said he believed the move would contribute to INA's plans to grow into a strong central European oil company and obtain a listing on the London Stock Exchange in 1999.

The company recently raised a five-year $100 million loan through a syndicate of foreign banks, led by Bankers Trust. The funds will be used for upgrading its refineries and filling stations and for new gas exploration projects in the Adriatic.
Matesa also confirmed that Nikola Kojakovic, who has been president of INA since December 1995, would become Croatia's new ambassador to Great Britain.
Local media have been speculating on the change at the helm of the country's largest firm for the past three weeks, but no official reaction was available until now. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
